title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S = k{T} is the divided-power polynomial algebra over k. It is graded with T^{(i)} in degree i, and T^{(a)}T^{(b)} = C(a+b,a) T^{(a+b)}. The previous page defines 'ombres virtuelles' (virtual shadows) of k-modules as graded S-modules. Inside this category it singles out the thick subcategories of N-negligible modules and of negligible modules, the latter meaning modules that are T^{(>>0)}-torsion elementwise. The Gabriel quotient by N-negligible modules is identified with modules concentrated in degrees >= N, and the quotient functor with truncation tau_N. That quotient functor has a right adjoint (section functor) phi_N, and phi_{0N} is presumably phi_N followed by restriction to degrees >= 0.

Theorem on this page: for any k-module M, the unit M⊗_k S -> phi_N tau_N(M⊗_k S) is an isomorphism in degrees >= 0. Equivalently, the 'free' shadows M⊗S lie in the essential image of phi_{0N} for every N, hence of phi_{0,omega} (the localization by all negligible objects). In modern terms, M⊗S is closed (saturated) with respect to the torsion theory, in degrees >= 0. Equivalently, the H^0 and H^1 'local cohomology' at the irrelevant ideal vanish in degrees >= 0. This is the analogue of Serre's Gamma_*(O(n)) = S_n for n >= 0, but for divided powers.

NB: in degrees >= N the claim is trivial, so only degrees 0 <= i < N matter. The case i = 0 was handled earlier.

Reformulation: for 0 <= i <= N, the map M = (M⊗S)_i -> Hom^i(tau_{N-i}S, M⊗S), xi |-> (multiplication by xi T^{(i)}), is bijective. In other words, every degree-i S-linear map from the ideal S_{>=N-i} into M⊗S extends uniquely to S.

Corollary as stated: Ext^n(tau_{N-i}(S)[-i], M⊗S) = 0 for n > 0.

Elimination of k: a degree-i map is determined by elements xi_k in M (k >= N), via T^{(k-i)} |-> xi_k T^{(k)}. S-linearity gives c_{l,k} xi_k = c_{l,k-i} xi_{k+l} with c_{l,k} = C(l+k,l). I checked this: T^{(l)}T^{(k-i)} = C(l+k-i,l)T^{(k+l-i)} on one side, and T^{(l)}·xi_k T^{(k)} = C(l+k,l) xi_k T^{(k+l)} on the other. The theorem becomes a purely arithmetic statement over Z: any such compatible family is of the form xi_k = C(k,i)·xi for a unique xi in M.

Proof on the next page: localize at each prime p. For k = i + p^m with p^m > i, Lucas gives C(k,i) ≡ 1 mod p, so gcd_{k>=N} C(k,i) = 1. A Bezout combination sum m_a C(k_a,i) = 1 then defines xi = sum m_a xi_{k_a}, which gives uniqueness. The relation is checked in each M_(p), where the local statement holds.

Purpose: this is a step in a theory of graded divided-power modules ('shadows') used for the divided-power de Rham complex (1976 IHES talk). It shows that the shadow functors omega_N are fully faithful on free objects and that free shadows are recovered from their truncations.
errors: The Corollary claims Ext^n(tau_{N-i}S[-i], M⊗S) = 0 for all n > 0, but the Theorem only gives the case n = 1. Equivalently, it gives Ext^1 (and Hom) of S/tau_{N-i}S. For n >= 2 one needs Ext^{n+1}(S/tau S, M⊗S) = 0. Over F_p the algebra Gamma(T) is a colimit of truncated polynomial (Frobenius) algebras and has infinite global dimension, so this is not automatic. It is plausibly true via local self-injectivity, but no argument is given here.
On the next page the binomial coefficient is written inconsistently: C_{i,k-i} in (2), but C_{k,k-i} in the gcd argument. The correct coefficient is C_{i,k-i} = binom(k,i).

The theorem is stated only for degrees >= 0, and that restriction is essential. Already for ordinary polynomial rings, restriction from S to S_{>=m} fails to be surjective in negative degrees. The text is consistent with this.

ideas.what: Category of graded modules over the divided-power polynomial algebra k{T} ('ombres virtuelles'), with truncation as Gabriel quotient by bounded/torsion modules and the section functor phi_N
ideas.modern_name: Quasi-coherent sheaves on G_a^#/G_m (graded Gamma(T)-modules); Serre-Gabriel localization of graded modules by torsion (QGr)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gabriel (1962) and Serre (FAC) for localization and section functors. The stack G_a^#/G_m and its graded divided-power modules appear in Drinfeld and Bhatt-Lurie (2020s, prismatization / Hodge-Tate stack).

ideas.what: Free shadows M⊗k{T} are saturated: Hom from S_{>=N-i} in degree i equals M (unique extension), i.e. vanishing of H^0, H^1 of local cohomology in degrees >= 0 for divided powers
ideas.modern_name: Depth/saturation of free modules over the divided-power algebra; Gamma_* computation for Proj of a divided-power algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (folklore-level; the analogous polynomial statement is due to Serre)

ideas.what: Reduction to integer combinatorics: compatible families c_{l,k}xi_k = c_{l,k-i}xi_{k+l} are of the form binom(k,i)xi; proof via the gcd of binom(k,i) over k >= N being 1 (Lucas) and local-global over Z_(p)
ideas.modern_name: Binomial interpolation / gcd of binomial coefficients, Lucas' theorem

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'ombres virtuelles' are graded k{T}-modules, i.e. in today's language quasi-coherent sheaves on G_a^#/G_m (the divided-power analogue of the Rees/filtration stack A^1/G_m). He studies their torsion localization and shows free objects are saturated. This category is central in recent prismatic and Hodge-Tate theory (conjugate filtrations, Sen operators). Grothendieck's 1976 divided-power de Rham notes anticipate working with such 'divided-power filtrations' as a category in their own right.
missed.quote: S = k{T} (polynômes à p.d.) anneau gradué à degrés ≥ 0 ... M⊗_k S ≅> φ_{0N} τ_N(M⊗_k S)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical precedent for the G_a^#/G_m formalism. His saturation lemma (unique extension from S_{>=N} in degrees >= 0) is a concrete statement about this stack's cohomology near the 'cone point' that could be compared with Bhatt-Lurie / Drinfeld computations.

missed.claim: The higher Ext-vanishing corollary (Ext^n = 0 for all n > 0) is asserted, but only the n = 1 case follows from the theorem as proved.
missed.quote: Cor Ext^n(τ_{N-i}(S)[-i], M⊗_k S) = 0 si n>0 ∀i≥0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small open check: vanishing of higher local cohomology for divided-power graded modules in nonnegative degrees. The answer is likely positive via the Frobenius (self-injective) structure of truncated divided powers.

deep.surprise_reason: Each individual step is elementary: a standard torsion localization plus a gcd/Lucas argument. What is mildly notable is the framework: an unpublished category of graded divided-power modules ('shadows') with truncation/section functors, which today would be read as sheaves on G_a^#/G_m. That object only became prominent decades later.
